messages:
irene: Heads-up — dedicated capacity dashboard for customer-123 in eu-west shows 0 GPUs for nodepool 'np-7' after we rolled back the pool at ~13:12 UTC. Customer ticket 9876 reports 503s and latency spikes.
deploy-bot: rollback completed: np-7 @ 2026-03-12T13:12:08Z (initiated by infra/auto-rollback).
sam: I can reproduce on the dashboard — list view and per-node breakdown both show 0 GPUs. Not seeing errors on the UI side.
kevin: Quick cluster check: `kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=np-7 -o wide` shows 4 nodes Ready and node labels look correct. `nvidia-smi` on one node shows GPUs present. So nodes are there.
maria: That suggests the inventory pipeline (metadata -> analytics) might be out of sync. On the metrics side `sum(inventory_gpus{pool="np-7"})` returns 0 in the analytics DB.
sam: Ran a quick curl to the internal inventory API: `curl -sS https://internal.inventory.prod/api/v1/pools/np-7` -> `{ "gpus": 0, "nodes": 4 }` — API is returning zero GPUs, even though nodes advertise GPUs.
kevin: I pulled logs from inventory-sync:```
kubectl logs deployment/inventory-sync -n infra | tail -n 50
2026-03-12T12:58:10Z ERROR failed to connect to metadata-db: dial tcp 10.11.22.33:5432: i/o timeout
2026-03-12T12:58:25Z WARN reconcile loop: partial failure, skipping pool np-7
2026-03-12T13:11:45Z INFO received pool-change event: rollback np-7
2026-03-12T13:12:01Z ERROR reconcile failed: null pointer
```
maria: Looks like inventory-sync hit DB/connect flakiness during the rollback window and wrote partial state (gpus=0). Analytics pulled that partial state and surfaced 0s.
support-ops: Customer-facing note: told customer we're investigating, asked for any recent deploys. They confirmed they saw the rollback at ~13:12 and traffic spike.
irene: Action plan: 1) try a controlled reconcile for np-7 2) if inventory-sync is unhealthy, restart it 3) backfill the analytics cluster from the node-reporter source.
sam: Running a manual reconcile now: `kubectl exec -it deploy/inventory-sync -n infra -- /bin/reconcile --pool np-7 --force`
kevin: While that's running, I checked the job controller — the inventory-sync deployment had OOMs and a crashloop earlier. I bumped its CPU/mem in a canary ns and redeployed.
maria: reconcile finished and returned success; I triggered a forced backfill: `POST https://internal.analytics.prod/admin/backfill?pool=np-7` -> 202 Accepted.
sam: Inventory API now returns correct GPU counts: `{ "gpus": 16, "nodes": 4 }` and dashboard panels are updating (seen GPU totals increase).
support-ops: Customer updated ticket: latency returned to normal and 503s stopped. Marking as mitigated.
irene: Root cause hypothesis: race between nodepool rollback events and inventory-sync reconcilers + transient DB connectivity caused a partial write (gpus=0). Follow-ups: postmortem, add guardrails so we never write zeroed GPU counts on partial failure, add alert for inventory-sync DB errors, increase liveness for inventory-sync to avoid crashloops during rollbacks.
kevin: I'll open an infra PR to add a transactional write + validation on GPU count > 0 unless pool is empty.
maria: I'll create an analytics job to detect sudden GPU drops >50% within 2 minutes and page eng-sre.
irene: Thanks — filing support ticket update and scheduling postmortem meeting. I'll add the corrective actions to the incident board. :white_check_mark:
